move: white fill floods button from cursor entry edge, arrow unfolds, retreats on exit
how: A two-line headline and an outlined pill button 'Get started' rise in with expo.out over the first 18% of the 4s loop while a cursor waits at bottom right. The cursor glides to the button's left edge with power3.inOut, and at 1.15s (29%) a 40px white circle positioned at that edge scales 0 to 12 with power3.out, flooding the button white; the label tweens to black, an arrow slot widens 0 to 34px with back.out(2) as the arrow slides in, the button lifts 4px at scale 1.04 and a soft glow appears. The cursor tracks across the button for 1.2s; at 2.55s the fill circle jumps to the right edge and collapses to scale 0 with power3.in, the label returns to white, the arrow folds, glow fades and the cursor retreats. At 3.6s headline and button exit upward staggered with power3.in so the frame is empty for the loop.
adapt: Change the headline, label and the white/black inversion colours; the fill entry and exit points are measured from the button's bounding rect so any button width works. Keep the 0.6s power3.out flood and the arrow's back.out(2) unfold.
port: mount(el, shot) builds headline, glow, button (fill circle, label, arrow slot) and cursor inside el, then reads the button rect relative to el. animate returns the timeline with flood at 0.2875D, glide 0.325D to 0.625D, retreat 0.65D, exit 0.9D. getBoundingClientRect must be taken relative to el, and the from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: cursor path uses getBoundingClientRect at build time, so layout must be final
